messages:
maria: dropped an nsys capture + perfetto slice here: https://artifacts.internal/trace/1845129876/run.nsys :eye_in_speech_bubble:

maria: high level: during steady-state inference we're seeing kernels on stream 0 idle while there's a long H2D activity on a different async stream (stream 7). timeline looks like memcpy dominates the copy engine and kernels pile up waiting. not sure if this is copy-engine saturation or CPU-side batching/prefetch pacing.

ajay: can you attach the trimmed timeline view (CUDA track + CPU threads + memcpy lanes)? also which CUDA driver/runtime version?

maria: runtime 12.2.0, driver 530.xx. here's the quick snippet i pasted from the timeline:```nsys timeline snippet
[stream 7] memcpy H2D 12.4 ms  (host staging pinned)
[stream 0] kernel forward 9.2 ms  (queued, waited 15.8 ms)
[stream 0] kernel attention 6.1 ms (queued)```

maria: also saw CPU thread 'kv_prefetcher' spike every 50ms and then immediately do multiple cudaMemcpyAsync calls, so prefetch bursts are bunched.
tomas: that pattern screams host-side batching of prefetch requests. if the prefetcher allocates pinned buffers per request we can easily saturate the copy engine plus the driver-side queuing. on some cards the copy engine serialization will make kernels on compute streams wait for the engine to free up.

karen: did you check whether the memcpy calls are cudaMemcpyAsync from pageable memory (which triggers driver staging) vs from already-pinned memory? nsys will often show an extra host-side memcpy if pageable->pinned fallback happens.

maria: i grep'd the codepath: prefetch uses a buffer pool but the pooling sometimes misses and falls back to malloc -> then we call cudaMemcpyAsync from a pointer that wasn't pinned. so yes, looks like fallback happening under heavy concurrency.
ajay: quick mitigation to test: force pooling to always pin (even if more mem) or throttle prefetch concurrency. can you repro with a smaller workload and run `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt -o p ./serve --kv-prefetch=true --prefetch-concurrency=8`? also collect `nvprof --print-gpu-trace` for comparison.

perf-bot: automated-alert: prefetched-host-to-device-throughput spiked to 8.1 GB/s between 1845129900 and 1845130100; copy-engine utilization 93% :warning:

maria: running the repro now. early observation: when i force prefetch-concurrency=1 the memcpy windows spread out and kernels stop waiting. when concurrency=16 they collapse into big H2D bursts.
tomas: that's consistent. two options: 1) change prefetcher to uniform rate limit (spread copies across batch window) 2) ensure prefetch always uses pinned staging buffers (avoid driver fallback). third option: move prefetch to a lower-priority stream with dedicated copy engine affinity if hardware supports it.
karen: small note: some GPUs have single copy engine; others have copy engines per link. best to probe with a matrix test across our supported instances. we should add an env toggle to prefer pinned fallback for experiments.
ajay: for tracing, also capture CPU scheduling: there's a pattern where the prefetcher sleeps (usleep) and then wakes, creating bunching. try `perf sched` or `trace-cmd` on the prefetcher thread to see if the sleeps align with kernel queue growth.
maria: i captured perfetto slice of CPU thread -> shows prefetcher sleeping ~20ms between bursts, wakes and issues 8 memcpy calls in a tight loop causing H2D burst. attaching the slice: https://artifacts.internal/perfetto/1845129876/slice.html

maria: next steps for me: 1) flip on forced pinned allocation in pool and re-run trace 2) implement a simple token-bucket to spread prefetch calls across the batch window and test impact on tail latency 3) add an nsight comparison run for a pinned vs pageable case.
karen: can you also run with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0` on a machine with pci-bandwidth monitor (nvidia-smi dmon) so we can correlate host->device bw with timeline gaps?
maria: will do. reassigning myself to followup and will post new trace (ts will be 1845134000-ish). thanks all :thumbsup:

ajay: nice detective work. if pinned pool + rate-limit fixes it we should bake defaults and add a perf regression test to catch reintroductions.
maria: ack, creating a small unit perf test that runs the repro and fails if kernel queue wait > 5ms p90.

maria: (later) posted new capture with pinned-pool enabled: https://artifacts.internal/trace/1845134201/run_pinned.nsys — early numbers: copy-engine util down to 46%, kernel wait reduced to <1ms p95.
